stories.label: UK's Green Party adopts 'Zionism is racism' policy
stories.summary: Members of the Green Party of England and Wales, meeting at conference in Brighton, passed a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism and backing a single Palestinian state. Lead with what the motion actually says and commits the party to, the vote margin if reported, and how leader Zack Polanski (who is Jewish) responded. The mechanism: this is a members' vote binding party policy, not a leadership statement, in a party now polling as a serious rival to Labour on the left — so say what changes in practice. Give the objection in its own words (the Movement for Progressive Judaism and other Jewish community leaders call it antisemitic and say it discriminates against Jewish supporters) and the proponents' case in theirs; the sentiment split between FT and MEE/Dawn/SCMP is the story's two readings, so attribute each. TRT World is Turkish state media; FT, Dawn and SCMP are the factual base. The MEE link is a live-blog entry — use it only for quotes. Dateline Brighton.

stories.label: 500 detained in Delhi on Day 3 of protests seeking CEC's exit; Thackerays lead Mumbai march
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 160 detentions at the Delhi march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (10-03) and the journalists' harassment complaints (this morning) — one clause each. The new development: on day three the number detained in Delhi rose to about 500, and the protest spread to Mumbai, where Uddhav and Raj Thackeray led a 'Garjana Morcha' demanding that the Special Intensive Revision of the voter rolls be scrapped and paper ballots replace EVMs; Mumbai police have filed an FIR over the march. Lead with the 500 and the spread to a second city. The mechanism: the SIR lets the Election Commission strike names from the rolls ahead of state elections, so the fight is over who is allowed to vote, and the state's answer so far is detention and criminal cases against organisers — say what the Commission and the government say in reply, and give figures on names removed only as the sources report them. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Chaos in Spain as anti-tourist protests turn into violent clashes
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-03 report on the marches after Congress rejected the Sánchez government's tenant protections (one clause). The new development: Saturday's protests ended in clashes with police in Valencia, and the defeat of the housing bill has opened the question of an early election — Al Jazeera asks whether Sánchez's minority government can survive it, and unions are talking of a general strike. Lead with the clashes (arrests and injuries only as reported) and the political consequence, not the crowd. The mechanism: rents are rising faster than wages while tourist lets take housing off the market, and a government without a majority has just shown it cannot legislate on it — say what Sánchez and his allies have said about an election and what the tenants' unions will do next. Use Al Jazeera for the facts and the politics; the Express is a tabloid ('chaos' and 'anti-tourist' are its words — the protests are about housing), and RT is Russian state media: take nothing from either that Al Jazeera, Yahoo Finance or News18 does not also report. Dateline Valencia, or Madrid if the reports centre there.

stories.label: India In Talks With Both Russia And Ukraine To End War: S Jaishankar
stories.summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India's approach to the Russia-Ukraine war has moved 'beyond advocacy' of dialogue and that New Delhi is in talks with both Moscow and Kyiv — the clearest signal yet that India may mediate. Lead with his exact words and what, concretely, India is doing (contacts, visits, proposals — only as reported); if it is words alone, say so. The mechanism: India is one of the few states with working ties to both sides and is the largest buyer of Russian seaborne crude, which gives it leverage with Moscow and exposes it to the US secondary sanctions Washington is weighing — so mediation is also self-interest. Say what Moscow and Kyiv have said in the past few days about India's role, as the reports give it. Context in one clause: the week's escalation in Kyiv (covered). Both sources are Indian; the feed carries no Russian or Ukrainian response to this statement, and the article should say so. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed in Israeli attacks since Gaza genocidal war
stories.summary: Ahead of World Teachers' Day (5 October), the Palestinian Education Ministry said Israel has killed more than 800 Palestinian teachers, injured over 3,300 and detained more than 170 since October 2023. Lead with the three figures and who counts them. The mechanism: killing and detaining teachers, on top of destroyed schools, removes the people an education system is rebuilt from — give the ministry's figures on schools, students and lost school years only as the statement states them, and say whether the count covers Gaza alone or the West Bank too. Not a re-run of this morning's Gaza City strike (one clause at most): this is the cumulative toll on one profession. Say whether a ceasefire is nominally in force, as the report gives it. The only source is TRT World, Turkish state media, relaying a Palestinian Authority ministry: attribute the figures to the ministry via TRT by name, and note that the feed carries no Israeli response. Dateline Ramallah, where the ministry sits, unless the report says otherwise.

stories.label: Yemeni government announces launch of operation against Houthis
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's report of government strikes on Sanaa and Saada (one clause). The new development is a decision: Yemen's internationally recognised government has formally announced an operation against the Houthis, saying it is moving 'from the stage of preparations to the stage of liberation' after exhausting peaceful options — while the Houthi military spokesman claims advances against Saudi-backed forces in al-Jawf. Lead with the declaration, who made it and what it commits to; then the Houthi claim, as a claim. The mechanism: the truce that froze Yemen's front lines is now over in name as well as in fact, inside the wider US-Iran war, and the people who pay are Yemenis in a country where most already depend on aid — give casualties and territory only as reported. Both sources are state media on opposite sides: TASS (Russian state agency, filing from Doha) for the government's announcement, Mehr (Iranian state-affiliated, which calls the Houthi forces 'the Yemeni Armed Forces' and their opponents 'mercenaries') for the Houthi claim. Attribute each by name, adopt neither's vocabulary, and say nothing here is independently confirmed. Dateline Aden, the government's seat, unless the report says otherwise.

stories.label: Sudan Doctors Network: Four civilians killed in RSF drone attacks on South Kordofan
stories.summary: Rapid Support Forces drone strikes on residential neighbourhoods of Dilling, South Kordofan, killed four civilians, including a child and a woman, the Sudan Doctors Network says. Lead with the dead, the town and the named actor — the RSF — and who is doing the counting: a doctors' network, because no state body is. The mechanism: Dilling has been under siege and drones now let the RSF hit a town it does not hold, so civilians are killed at home with no front line near them; give the number injured, the dates of the strikes and the state of the town's hospital and supplies only as Radio Dabanga reports. Say what the network demands and whether the RSF has responded. Dateline Dilling.

stories.label: Security prosecution detains Abu Emaira for 15 days, whereabouts of 5 other Matsda2sh journalists unknown
stories.summary: Follow-up to the disputed detention order for six Matsda2sh journalists and the open-ended sit-in at the Journalists Syndicate (both covered 10-03 — one clause each). The new development: one of the six has surfaced. Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira was brought before Egypt's Supreme State Security Prosecution at 10 pm on Saturday, five days after his arrest, and given a 15-day detention order, an Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights lawyer told Mada Masr; the other five are still unaccounted for. Lead with the first appearance and the five still missing. The mechanism: five days of unacknowledged custody before any prosecutor is seen is enforced disappearance in practice, and State Security Prosecution's renewable 15-day orders can hold a journalist for years without trial — say what he is accused of, as the lawyer reports it. Matsda2sh is a fact-checking platform: say what it published. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Hailstorms destroy 3,750 farms in South Darfur
stories.summary: Hailstorms destroyed at least 3,750 farms in the Daous area north-west of Kass, South Darfur, the locality's executive director told Radio Dabanga. Lead with the number of farms and what was growing on them, weeks before harvest. The mechanism: in a region where war has already cut planting, markets and aid access, a lost harvest is not replaced — these families have no insurance, no state compensation and limited relief, so say which crops were lost, how many people depend on them and what help the official asked international organisations for, strictly as reported. Who administers Kass (South Darfur is under RSF control) matters for whether aid can reach it: state it if the report does. A disaster report with consequences for hunger, not a weather story. Dateline Kass.

stories.label: US doesn't rule out imposing secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners by Oct. 18
stories.summary: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the administration does not rule out deciding by 18 October to impose secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners, under the sanctions law Trump signed on 18 September. Lead with the date and whom it lands on: not Russia but the countries that buy its oil — India, China and Turkey above all — whose refiners and banks would have to choose between Russian crude and access to the US market. The mechanism: say what the law requires by that date and what discretion the president keeps, as the report gives it; with Hormuz restricted, discounted Russian barrels are what several importers are leaning on, so the threat bears on Brent crude as well as on Moscow's revenue. Wright's remarks are a statement, not a decision — write them as such, and include his line that ending the war would lower energy prices only as attributed. The only source is TASS, Russian state media, reporting a US official's remarks: attribute by name and say where he made them. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Fuel supply stable despite South Pars output drop: NIGC
stories.summary: The head of the National Iranian Gas Company, Saeid Tavakoli, acknowledged that production at South Pars — the field that supplies most of Iran's natural gas — fell in the first six months of the Iranian year, while saying deliveries to power plants and industry held. Lead with the admission, not the reassurance: give the size of the drop and its stated cause if he gives them, and say so plainly if he does not. The mechanism: South Pars feeds Iran's power stations, industry and home heating, so lower output heading into winter means the choice between cutting industry, burning dirtier liquid fuel in power plants or rationing households — say how the company claims it kept supply stable (storage, fuel switching, cuts elsewhere) as reported. One clause of context: the war and the US blockade. The only source is Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency, quoting a state company about its own performance: attribute every figure to Tavakoli via Mehr, and state none of the 'stable supply' claim as fact. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: One giant clam contains a month‑by‑month diary of the Great Barrier Reef's climate 200 years ago
stories.summary: Researchers have read a month-by-month record of the Great Barrier Reef's climate about 200 years ago from the shell of a single giant clam. Lead with what the shell recorded and for how long. The mechanism is the story: a giant clam lays down shell in fine growth bands, and the chemistry of each band (oxygen isotopes and trace elements, as the report specifies) fixes the temperature and conditions of the water it grew in — so one shell gives monthly resolution from before instrument records began, where corals and ice cores give coarser or more distant readings. Say how the shell was dated, what the record shows about reef conditions then against now, and name the team and the journal as Phys.org gives them. A finding, not a nature piece: skip the scene-setting about swimming over the reef. The feed entry is a teaser — use only what the page states. Dateline as the report gives the research institution; Townsville or Cairns only if stated.

stories.label: OPEC+ seven keep November oil production plan unchanged
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's preview of the OPEC+ meeting (one clause). The new development is the decision: the seven producers making voluntary cuts — Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Oman and Algeria — kept their November production plan unchanged, and the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee, meeting online, reviewed July and August output, voiced concern over attacks on energy infrastructure and set its next meeting for 29 November. Lead with the unchanged quota and give the figures as reported. The mechanism: Bloomberg's delegates say the war has shut in swaths of the group's output, so a quota on paper no longer describes the barrels that reach buyers through the Strait of Hormuz — the cartel is holding a number it cannot fill, and Russia's Novak calls the market tense with a supply deficit. That gap is what moves Brent crude. TASS is Russian state media and Russia is a party to the deal: attribute its reports by name; Bloomberg is the independent source. One article from all the reports in `sources`. Dateline Vienna, or as the reports give it.

stories.label: Tether Brings Its $184 Billion Stablecoin Back to Bitcoin: Will BTC Regain Its Role as a Payments Network? - AOL
stories.summary: Tether is relaunching USDT, its $184 billion dollar stablecoin, on bitcoin this month, twelve years after it left the network for faster and cheaper chains such as Tron and Ethereum. Lead with the return and the size of the token. The mechanism a technical reader wants: the relaunch uses the RGB protocol, which keeps most USDT transaction data off bitcoin's main chain, so the network gains a dollar payments layer while its miners collect almost no fees from it — say what is settled on-chain and what is not. Who it lands on: stablecoins are how people in high-inflation economies hold dollars, so say where USDT is actually used, as the report gives it. The headline's question is the outlet's; do not answer it, and leave out any investment framing or price forecast. AOL is carrying a syndicated markets piece: use its facts, attribute claims about adoption to Tether. Dateline San Salvador, where Tether is based, unless the report says otherwise; not a US dateline.

stories.label: Trump names AI czar to head White House task force
stories.summary: Trump on Sunday announced a White House task force to coordinate the administration's response to artificial intelligence and named Jay Clayton, a lawyer and former securities regulator, to lead it as AI czar. Do not write an appointment notice. Lead with who was chosen and what the body can actually do — whether it has authority over agencies, budgets or rules, or only coordinates — and who else sits on it (the Director of National Intelligence is tagged), as DW reports. The mechanism: the appointment follows a week in which OpenAI disclosed an intrusion by misaligned agents and lost safety staff (covered 10-02 and 10-04 — one clause), and data centres became a midterm liability in Ohio; the administration's answer is a coordinator from finance and prosecution, not a regulator with powers over the companies. Say what the task force is charged with and by when, and what it is not. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Moscow vows to ramp up strikes on Ukraine after Zelensky's threat -- RT Russia & Former Soviet Union
stories.summary: Follow-up to Zelensky's pledge to hit Russian energy sites (10-03) and the strike on Kyiv's Northern Bridge during Merz's visit (this morning) — one clause each. The new development: Russia's Defence Ministry has now said on the record that its massive strikes on Kyiv and other regions are a response to Zelensky, and that it will step them up against what it calls military and defence-industry facilities. Lead with the ministry's statement as a declared policy of escalation, quoted. The mechanism: each side now names the other's statements as the reason for its next strike, and Moscow's description of its targets as military sits against a bridge and housing hit in a city of millions — set the ministry's words beside what was actually struck, using only what earlier reports established. Both sources are Russian state media (TASS and RT): attribute everything to the ministry via them by name, state none of its claims as fact, and say the feed carries no Ukrainian or independent account of this statement. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Spain floods: 2 dead as heavy rain hits Catalonia
stories.summary: Torrential rain and flooding have left two people dead and one missing in Catalonia, Deutsche Welle reports, after forecasters warned of a Mediterranean 'mini-hurricane' bringing more than 200 litres of rain per square metre in about six hours. Lead with the dead and the missing — who and where (Tordera and Montornès del Vallès are tagged) — taking the toll from DW, the latest of the three reports; the Euro Weekly News and Anadolu pieces are the warnings from the day before. The mechanism: Meteocat forecast the storm and Civil Protection had the ES-Alert phone warning ready, so say whether and when the alert was sent and what people were told to do — after Valencia in 2024 the question in Spain is not whether the rain was predicted but whether the warning reached people in time. A disaster report, not a science story: no climate attribution unless a source makes it. Anadolu is Turkish state media; DW is the factual base. Dateline Tordera, or Barcelona if DW files from there.

stories.label: Security forces kill 8 terrorists in Dera Ismail Khan IBO: state media
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed eight people they describe as militants of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan in an intelligence-based operation in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, according to security sources quoted by state-run Radio Pakistan and carried by Dawn. Lead with the eight dead and exactly who says so: the account comes from unnamed security sources through state radio, with no independent confirmation of who the dead were — say that plainly, and note that 'Fitna al Khawarij' is the state's own term for the TTP, as Dawn explains. The mechanism: these operations are reported only by the force that carries them out, in the same province whose government is today marching on Islamabad (PTI march, covered this morning — one clause), so the public record of the war in KP is a series of military statements. Give any figures Dawn has on recent attacks and operations in the district. Dateline Dera Ismail Khan.

stories.label: Inka scattered sacred coca leaves over sacrificed llamas, excavation suggests
stories.summary: Archaeologists excavating Tambo Viejo, an Inka provincial centre in Peru's Acarí Valley, have found coca leaves still caught in the wool of sacrificed llamas — the first direct evidence of how the Inka used one of their most sacred plants in ritual, where until now there were only a few seeds and stored leaves. Lead with the leaves in the wool and what they show: coca was scattered over the animals as part of the sacrifice. The mechanism: say how the find was made and dated, how the leaves were identified, and why it matters — Spanish chroniclers described coca offerings, but physical evidence rarely survives, and the dry coast preserved it; give the journal and the team as Phys.org reports them. The site's tasselled llamas and adorned guinea pigs get one clause. A finding, not a travel piece. Dateline Acarí, Peru.

stories.label: Germany's Merz Arrives in Kyiv, Warns of Putin's Threat to West
stories.summary: Follow-up to Russia's warning to diplomats to leave Kyiv and Zelensky's pledge to hit Russian refineries (both covered 10-03 — one clause each). The new development: Russian forces struck one of Kyiv's main bridges, the Northern Bridge, on Sunday while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was in the city pledging further aid. Lead with the strike on the bridge and the fact that a head of government was in the capital a day after Moscow told foreigners to get out — then what Merz actually committed (sums, weapons, dates) as Bloomberg and SCMP report it, not his rhetoric. The mechanism: the Dnipro bridges are what hold a city of millions together, so hitting them is the 'make Kyiv unliveable' policy Zelensky described, and the visit is Berlin's answer to the evacuation warning. Give casualties and damage only as reported; the Mirror is a tabloid — take facts from Bloomberg, SCMP and TRT World (Turkish state media, carrying Reuters). Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: PTI set to begin its protest march from KP's Lakki Marwat today
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-03 report that the long march would go ahead pending a second round of talks (one clause). The new development: the talks between the federal government and the opposition failed, and the PTI march demanding the release of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan sets off today from Lakki Marwat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa towards Islamabad, which is bracing for it. Lead with the collapse of the talks and the march starting — who leads it (the KP chief minister, as Dawn names him), the route, and what the government has done in the capital (containers, Section 144, arrests, mobile shutdowns — only as reported). The mechanism: the party governs one province and uses its machinery to march on a federal capital that holds its leader in Adiala jail, so each march is a contest between a provincial government and the centre, not just a street protest. Say what each side offered in the talks and why they broke down. Dateline Lakki Marwat, or Peshawar if Dawn files from there.

stories.label: Four women among five killed in Israeli strike on Gaza
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-03 item on a Gaza hospital reporting five killed, which ran from a wire round-up with almost no detail (one clause). What is new: the dead are now identified and the toll has risen — an Israeli airstrike on an apartment building in Gaza City early Saturday killed at least five Palestinians, four of them women, among them a Christian mother, Maisa Abu Dawoud, and her daughter Mary, as medics and the church confirmed; The National reports six killed in strikes across Gaza. Lead with the names and who they were, the building that was hit, and the count from each source, stating plainly which figure covers what. Then what the Israeli military said it was targeting, and the mechanism: say whether a ceasefire is nominally in force and what continues under it, strictly as Dawn (Reuters copy) and The National report. Name the actor; no 'exchange of fire' framing unless the sources report one. Dateline Gaza City.

stories.label: Iranian Foreign Ministry confirms discussions on possible withdrawal from NPT
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said at his Sunday briefing that serious discussions are under way in Tehran about leaving the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, while stressing that Iran remains a party for now and that the ministry will follow whatever the competent authorities decide. Lead with the confirmation and both halves of it — discussed, not decided. The mechanism: the NPT is the legal basis for IAEA inspections, so withdrawal (Article X, three months' notice) would end the outside world's view into a programme holding a stockpile of 60% enriched uranium, in the middle of a war and truce talks with Washington; say who in Iran would take the decision, as the report gives it. The sources are TASS (Russian state media) and Mehr (Iranian state-affiliated): attribute by name, quote Baghaei's words, state nothing about Iran's intentions as fact. His other remarks (the US as UN host, an expelled diplomat) get one clause at most. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Three Women Journalists Accuse Police Personnel Of Sexual Harassment During Jantar Mantar Protest
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-03 report that Delhi Police detained 160 people at the march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (one clause). The new development: three women journalists covering that protest at Jantar Mantar have accused police personnel of sexually harassing them, and Delhi Police has transferred the complaints to its Crime Branch for a formal enquiry. Lead with the accusation and the enquiry — what the journalists say happened, which outlets they work for if named, and whether an FIR has been registered or only an internal enquiry opened; these are allegations, so attribute every detail. The mechanism: the force accused is investigating itself, and the complainants were reporters documenting how a protest over voter rolls was policed — say what press bodies and opposition figures (Rahul Gandhi is tagged) have demanded, and what the police say. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Video: Cornell President Calls Allegations 'Deeply Disturbing'
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-03 report that the district attorney declined to review additional evidence in the 2024 fraternity rape case at Cornell (one clause). The new development: after a week of outrage the university's president, Michael Kotlikoff, addressed it publicly for the first time in an eight-minute video, calling what happened to 'Jane Doe' deeply disturbing and promising transparency and a 'serious look' at fraternities. Do not write a statement report. Lead with what he concretely committed to — an outside review, release of records, suspension or closure of fraternities, a timetable — and what he did not; if the reports show only words, say so. The mechanism: the university ran the 2024 investigation itself and prosecutors declined to act, so the institution is now judging its own handling; give Governor Hochul's intervention and the students' demands as the Guardian and Al Jazeera report them. The NYT link is a video page — take the facts from the Guardian and Al Jazeera texts. Dateline Ithaca. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions
stories.summary: Three Iranian officials set out Tehran's terms for the Strait of Hormuz on the same day: parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the strait stays shut until Washington meets seven conditions; foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said reopening would take no more than a week if the US accepts Iran's settlement plan; and spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the strait the 'main focus' of the truce talks. One article from all three. Lead with the seven conditions — list them as reported — and the seven-day reopening offer, then the mechanism: Iran is pricing the reopening of the waterway against the lifting of the US blockade, so ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and with it Brent crude, now hangs on a negotiation rather than on the fighting. Say where the talks stand and who mediates (Islamabad is tagged), only as the reports give it. Earlier coverage (tankers struck 10-03, Iraq's state tanker passage) gets one clause. Middle East Eye is the independent base; the Araghchi remarks come via TASS, Russian state media — attribute them by name. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Kemi Badenoch publishes bombshell document setting out Tory plans
stories.summary: On the first day of the Conservative conference in Birmingham, Kemi Badenoch published a policy document, 'The Right Way', that Bloomberg reports eyes abolishing UK inheritance tax and removing the childcare 'cliff edge' — the income threshold at which parents abruptly lose support. Write it as an economy story, not a conference report. Lead with the two concrete proposals and what each would cost and whom it would benefit, using the sources' figures only: inheritance tax is paid by a small share of estates, so say who gains from abolition and what revenue is forgone, and explain how the childcare threshold produces a marginal tax rate above 100% for the families who cross it. The mechanism: an opposition squeezed between Burnham's Labour and Reform UK is competing on tax cuts without stating how they are funded — say whether the document gives costings or only principles. The Express is a partisan tabloid ('bombshell' is its word); take the substance from Bloomberg. Dateline Birmingham.

stories.label: Nestle dairy whitener found unsafe, substandard by FSSAI; Nestle says product safe
stories.summary: India's food regulator, FSSAI, said on Saturday that a sample of Nestlé India's Low Fat Dairy Whitener, collected from The LaLiT hotel in Connaught Place, New Delhi, was declared 'unsafe and substandard' by a food analyst's laboratory; Nestlé says the product is safe. Lead with the finding and exactly what the laboratory found — which parameter failed and by how much — and Nestlé's response, each attributed. The mechanism: say what 'unsafe' versus 'substandard' mean under India's Food Safety and Standards Act, what happens next (the company's right to a referral-laboratory retest, penalties, recall), and whether the result binds one batch or the product line. A multinational's product failing a national regulator's test is an accountability story only if the process is explained; mention Nestlé's earlier Indian cases (Maggi 2015) only if the report does. One sample, one lab: do not generalise beyond it. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Sanaa, Riyadh rattled by strikes as war widens
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-02 report that Riyadh was planning an offensive against the Houthis and the 10-03 fire near an Aramco site in Riyadh (one clause each). The new development: forces of Yemen's internationally recognised government say they are striking Houthi targets in Sanaa and the group's northern stronghold of Saada, amid reported Saudi strikes on the capital, and the Houthis have claimed the Aramco attack. Lead with the strikes on Sanaa and who says they carried them out, then the Houthi claim. Count and identify any dead and say what was hit, as Reuters and The National report it; say plainly what is claimed by each side (Al-Masirah is the Houthis' own channel) and what is independently confirmed. The mechanism: the Yemen front, quiet since the truce, has reopened inside the wider US-Iran war, and Yemenis in a city of millions are again under air attack while the Houthis answer on Saudi oil infrastructure. TRT World is Turkish state media; Reuters, Dawn and The National are the independent base. Dateline Sanaa, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Burnham scraps controversial plans to curb jury trials
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has dropped the plan, introduced under Keir Starmer, to let judges alone decide cases carrying a likely sentence of under three years; the Ministry of Justice says only complex fraud cases would still be affected (state the remaining carve-out exactly as the BBC and Reuters do). Lead with the reversal and what the scrapped proposal would have removed: the right to be tried by a jury for a large class of offences. The mechanism: the curb was the government's answer to a record Crown Court backlog, so abandoning it after a backlash from lawyers and Labour MPs leaves the backlog — and the defendants and victims waiting years for trial — where it was; say what the government now proposes instead and give the backlog figure if the sources do. Dateline London.

stories.label: Japan Protests After U.S. Marine Is Accused of Killing Woman in Okinawa
stories.summary: Japan's government lodged a rare formal protest with the United States on Sunday after a US Marine was arrested in connection with the death of a woman in Okinawa. Lead with the death, the arrest and the protest — who the woman was and what the Marine is accused of, strictly as the report states; it is an accusation, not a conviction. The mechanism: Okinawa hosts the bulk of US forces in Japan on a fraction of its land, and under the Status of Forces Agreement custody and jurisdiction over American personnel are negotiated rather than automatic, so each killing reopens the question of who answers to Japanese courts — say who holds the suspect now, what Tokyo demanded and what the US military said. Mention earlier cases only if the source does. Dateline Naha, or Tokyo if the report places the protest there; not a US dateline.

stories.label: Brazil to hold first round of presidential election
stories.summary: Brazil votes today, Sunday 4 October, in the first round of its general election: the presidency, the governors of every state and the Federal District, the whole Chamber of Deputies and a third of the Senate. Lead with the vote and what is decided today, and the rule that matters — a candidate needs more than half the valid votes or the top two go to a run-off; give the run-off date and the candidates and poll figures only if the source states them. Earlier coverage gets one clause: the final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and the US and Australia closed consulates. Polls are open as this is written: report no result. The only source in the feed is Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency, so attribute the report to it by name; the facts here are the electoral calendar, not a contested claim. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Trump Promotes Data Centers at Rally With Republican Facing Heat on Them
stories.summary: Campaigning in Ohio on Saturday for Republican senator Jon Husted, Trump defended the data centres that power the AI industry — the issue that has become a liability for Husted in his race against Democrat Sherrod Brown. Do not write a rally report. Lead with the fact that AI data centres are now unpopular enough to threaten a Senate seat, and that the president chose to defend them anyway. The mechanism: the complexes draw electricity and water at a scale that residents see in their bills and their land, while the jobs and the profits go elsewhere, so the costs of the AI build-out have become a ballot issue a month before the midterms — give the sources' figures on Ohio power prices, the number of sites and the polling only as reported. Quote what Trump said about them and what Brown says. Dateline the Ohio city the reports name, not Washington.

stories.label: North Korean hypersonic missile hits target 1,000 km away -- news agency
stories.summary: North Korea says it launched a 'strategic' intermediate-range hypersonic missile that hit a target 1,000 km away in the Sea of Japan, in a drill Kim Jong Un observed in person. The chain of sourcing is state media twice over — KCNA, North Korea's agency, relayed by TASS, Russia's — so attribute every detail to KCNA via TASS by name and state none of the missile's performance as fact; the feed carries no confirmation from Seoul or Tokyo, and the article should say so. Lead with the launch, the claimed range and Kim's presence, then what KCNA says the drill was for. The mechanism in one paragraph: an intermediate-range missile with a manoeuvring warhead is aimed at US bases in Japan and Guam, not at Seoul, and a manoeuvring warhead is built to defeat the interceptors those bases rely on. Recent context (Seoul's dispute with Kyiv over North Korean prisoners of war) gets one clause at most. Dateline Pyongyang.

stories.label: OPEC+ Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee to review oil market situation
stories.summary: OPEC+ ministers meet on Sunday 4 October: the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee reviews the oil market and members' compliance with the output agreement, alongside the group of seven producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Oman and the others the report names — that sets monthly production. Lead with the meeting and what is on the table, as TASS reports it; the meeting has not happened yet, so report no decision. The mechanism: the cartel is setting quotas while its Gulf members cannot ship freely — tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz this week and Saudi oil sites are under attack — so a quota on paper and barrels that actually reach buyers have come apart, and that gap is what moves Brent crude. Say which members are over or under their quotas if the report does. This bears on Brent crude and on ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The only source is TASS, Russian state media, and Russia is a party to the agreement: attribute by name. Dateline Vienna, or as the report gives it.

stories.label: OpenAI safety leader quits, warning AI company's culture is 'broken'
stories.summary: David Robinson, a safety leader at OpenAI, has resigned, saying the company's culture is broken and that AI firms are not 'being nearly careful enough'; he argues the industry needs layered safety of the kind used in aviation and nuclear power instead of trial and error. Follow-up context in one clause: OpenAI fired two safety researchers and notified about 100 organisations of an intrusion by misaligned agents (both covered 10-02) — this is a third departure from the safety side in a week, and a voluntary one. Lead with who he is, what he ran and his exact words, then the mechanism a technical reader wants: what specific practices he says are missing (independent checks, redundancy, incident reporting) and why a company racing competitors has no outside body able to require them. Give OpenAI's response. Report his claims as his. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
stories.summary: The German AI company Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, which it calls a 'sovereign' open-weight language model; the announcement drew 547 points and 308 comments on Hacker News. Lead with what was released and under what terms — parameter count, licence, what 'open-weight' covers (weights, not necessarily training data or code), where it was trained and on whose hardware — as the company's post states. The mechanism: 'sovereign' is a claim about dependency — a model a European government or firm can run on its own machines without a US provider's API, terms or export rules — so say what in the stack is actually European and what is not (chips, cloud, data). The source is the company's own blog: attribute benchmarks to Aleph Alpha and say they are not independently verified. Dateline Heidelberg, where the company is based, unless the post says otherwise.

stories.label: US court halts AI nude-image ban challenged by Musk -- RT World News
stories.summary: A US federal appeals court has blocked Minnesota's law banning AI-generated fake nude images while Elon Musk's xAI challenges it as a violation of free-speech protections. Lead with the order: which court, what the law prohibited and whom it bound (the companies whose tools make the images, not only the people who post them), and what stays unenforced for now. The mechanism: the people harmed are those — mostly women and girls — whose likeness is stripped without consent, and the company whose image generator does it is arguing that the First Amendment protects the tool; an early win at the appeals level sets the terms for every other state drafting the same law. This is a preliminary block, not a final ruling — say so, and give Minnesota's response. The only source is RT, Russian state media: attribute the report to it by name and use only the court facts, none of its framing. Dateline St. Paul, or the court's seat if the report names it.

stories.label: Moscow unveils new doctrine targeting Ukrainian civilians, Zelensky vows to respond with more energy strikes
stories.summary: Follow-up to Russia's warning to diplomats to leave Kyiv and the strikes that killed six (covered 14:00 — one clause). The new development: Zelensky told Reuters on 3 October that Ukraine will step up strikes on Russian energy infrastructure in answer to what he calls a new Russian policy of air strikes on civilians, citing documents he says Ukrainian intelligence obtained — and Newsweek reports he is doing so despite an appeal from Trump to stop hitting refineries. Lead with the decision to escalate and whom it defies, then the mechanism: each side now names the other's civilian-supporting infrastructure as the target, and Ukrainian hits on Russian refineries land on a fuel market already short of diesel. Attribute the documents' contents to Zelensky — they are his claim, not an established fact. RT is Russian state media and carries Moscow's framing (Zelensky 'lashing out' at Western backers over a loan); use it only for what Russia says, with the Kyiv Independent and Newsweek as the factual base. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Iraq says it transported 2 million barrels of crude through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company carried 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude through the Strait of Hormuz aboard a very large crude carrier, which its director general called the company's first such operation in decades — on the same day two other tankers were struck by projectiles in the strait (covered 14:00 — one clause). Lead with the cargo, the ship and 'first in decades'. The mechanism: with Iran's blockade in force and foreign owners and insurers pulling back, an exporter that depends on Hormuz for almost all its oil revenue is moving its own crude on its own state-flagged hull, and Baghdad's relations with Tehran are what get a ship through where others are hit. Say where the cargo was bound and under what arrangement it passed, only as Reuters reports. This bears on ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and on Brent crude. Dateline Baghdad, or Basra if the source places the statement there.

stories.label: Why we can't strike despite locating kidnapped NYSC members - Police
stories.summary: Gunmen abducted about 19 prospective National Youth Service Corps members at about 6:30 am on Thursday on the Owerri-Onitsha road near Umunoha in Imo State, and the state police now say they know where the captives are held but cannot move in. Lead with the 19 young graduates taken on their way to compulsory national service and the police admission. The mechanism: give the police's stated reasons for holding back (the feed tags improvised explosives and drones — use only what the commissioner is quoted saying), and what that shows — the state sends graduates across the country by road for a mandatory scheme and cannot secure the highway or retrieve them once taken. Say who the abductors are thought to be only as the police say, whether a ransom has been demanded, and what the NYSC and the families have said. Dateline Owerri.

stories.label: Leaders of Peter Obi's support groups released after 24-hour detention
stories.summary: Akwa Ibom police released Elijah Noah and Ben Smith, leaders of the Obi-Kwankwaso and Obidient movements in the state, after more than 24 hours in detention over a disputed Independence Day march in Uyo. Lead with the detention of opposition organisers for a march on the national holiday and their release — say whether they were charged, on what legal ground they were held, and whether tear gas was used on the marchers, as Premium Times reports. The mechanism: ahead of the 2027 election, police permission decides which political gatherings are lawful, and a day in a cell without charge is a cost imposed on organising for the opposition without a court ever being asked. Give the police account alongside the movement's. Dateline Uyo.

stories.label: Trump ramps up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching
stories.summary: Trump spent more than 700 words on Truth Social on Saturday attacking Republican senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas for blocking the Sunshine Protection Act, which would end the twice-yearly clock change, and published what he said was the senator's mobile phone number. Lead with the president posting a sitting senator's number to tens of millions of followers, not with the clocks. The mechanism: a single senator's objection can stall a bill in the Senate, and the president's answer is not a vote but directing his followers at one member of his own party weeks before the midterms. Say what the bill does, why Cotton objects, and what Cotton and Senate leaders have said. No adjectives about the posts — quote them. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Russia, Iran attach much importance to cooperation in defense -- Medvedev
stories.summary: Dmitry Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, is in Tehran in the middle of the US-Iran war and said Russia and Iran are developing joint work in defence, aerospace, energy and artificial intelligence, called Iran the key to security in the Strait of Hormuz 'in terms of geography and international law', and said Moscow wants Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb to function normally. The only source is TASS, Russian state media: attribute every statement to Medvedev and to TASS by name, and state no cooperation as fact. Lead with the visit itself — who he met and what, if anything, was signed — and say plainly if the reports give only remarks and no agreement. The mechanism: Russia is backing Iran's legal claim to control the strait while saying it wants the strait open, which gives Tehran diplomatic cover without Moscow committing to its defence. His conditions for a Ukraine settlement, from the same trip, get one clause at most. One article from the three TASS reports in `sources`. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: How a farmers’ protest in Bucharest was inflated online, then hijacked
stories.summary: An analysis of more than 1,180 Facebook posts and 100 TikTok videos shows how a genuine farmers' protest in Bucharest was amplified by clusters of accounts posting identical messages and then folded into anti-government, anti-EU and pro-Kremlin narratives. Lead with the numbers and the finding, then the mechanism a technical reader wants: how the clusters were identified (identical text, timing, account networks), what the real protest was about, and at what point the framing was swapped — the operation did not invent a grievance, it attached itself to a real one. Say who did the analysis and with what method, what Meta and TikTok did or did not do, and what the analysis cannot show about who ran the accounts. Do not attribute the network to a state unless the report does. Dateline Bucharest.

stories.label: Feeling secure in a group may help dissenters make stronger arguments
stories.summary: A research team at KAIST in South Korea finds that group members who feel securely accepted voice dissent in more detail and more persuasively, and that the rest of the group is then more willing to use those objections in its decision. Lead with the finding and give the journal, the sample size and the experimental design as Phys.org reports them. The mechanism: say what the researchers think links belonging to the quality of an objection — and why that runs against the assumption that the outsider is the one who speaks freely — only as far as the study does, and what it could not measure (laboratory groups versus real organisations). A finding, not management advice: no second-person guidance. The feed entry is a teaser; if the page does not give the journal and method, say what is missing. Dateline Daejeon.

stories.label: Who is the mystery co-pilot behind the Flydubai attack?
stories.summary: Follow-up to the Flydubai cockpit attack and the UAE official's 'terror act' statement (covered — one clause). The new development: media reports, including the New York Times, identify the co-pilot as an Omani national who had previously been barred from flying in Oman over concerns about alleged extremist views — and there is still no official confirmation of his identity. Lead with the identification and who reported it, then the mechanism: a pilot grounded by one Gulf regulator was hired and cleared to fly by an airline in the next state, so the question is what vetting and information-sharing exists between Gulf aviation authorities. Say plainly what is reported versus confirmed, and what the UAE, Oman and Flydubai have said. Dateline Dubai, not Tel Aviv.

stories.label: IYC holds protest against detention of students in Delhi
stories.summary: Follow-up to the Mumbai Shivaji Park protest and the ultimatum to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (covered this morning — one clause). The new development: Delhi Police on Saturday detained 160 protesters during a march against the election commissioner, among them senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, activist Yogendra Yadav, AISA president Neha Bora and Anjali Bhardwaj, and Yadav has called a further march for October 4. Lead with the 160 detentions and the names, then the mechanism: the dispute is over the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls, and the state's answer to a protest about who gets to vote was to detain lawyers and student leaders in the capital — which widened it, with the Youth Congress now protesting the detentions themselves. Say where they were held, whether they were released, and what police gave as the legal ground. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Co-pilot in FlyDubai attack is identified, and other Mideast developments
stories.summary: This is a wire round-up; write ONE article and NOT the Flydubai item, which is a separate story this cycle. Lead with the Gaza item: a hospital in Gaza says Israeli strikes killed five people. Name the actor (Israel) and count and identify the dead as far as the report does — who they were, where the strikes hit, which hospital received them, and what the Israeli military said. The mechanism: say what the killings show about the state of the Strip now — whether a ceasefire is nominally in force, and what continues regardless — strictly as the report states it. The Flydubai identification gets no more than one clause. If the page gives too little on Gaza to stand as an article, say so rather than padding from the other items. Dateline the city in Gaza the report names.

stories.label: Dozens join syndicate demonstration to call for Matsda2sh journalists’ release
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's story on the disputed detention order for six Matsda2sh journalists (one clause). The new development: dozens of journalists held a sit-in inside Egypt's Journalists Syndicate on Saturday, and when it was due to end at 5 pm several members of the general assembly announced they would stay inside — an open-ended occupation of the syndicate — while the six, arrested on Monday, remain at an unknown location. Lead with the sit-in turning open-ended and the fact that five days on no authority has said where the six are. The mechanism: with no published order there is nothing to appeal, so the syndicate building is the one place the profession can apply pressure; say what the protesters demand, what the syndicate's board has done, and any response from the prosecution, strictly as Mada Masr reports. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Thousands of Germans demonstrators oppose rearmament, urge dialogue with Russia
stories.summary: On German Unity Day thousands marched in Berlin and Stuttgart against the possible return of military conscription and Germany's rearmament; police put the Berlin crowd at about 5,800. The only source is TASS, Russian state media, with an obvious interest in the story: attribute the report to it by name, use the police figure rather than any organisers' claim, and leave out TASS's framing about 'dialogue with Russia' except as a quoted demand of the marchers. Lead with the police count and what the demonstrators oppose, then the mechanism: Germany is debating bringing back conscription and is spending at a scale unseen since the Cold War, and those who would be drafted are the ones on the street — say who organised the marches and what stage the conscription law is at, only as far as the report supports it. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: Ex-Sheriff's Deputy Acquitted in Fatal Shooting of Airman Roger Fortson
stories.summary: A Florida jury on Friday acquitted former sheriff's deputy Eddie Duran of manslaughter in the 2024 killing of US Air Force airman Roger Fortson, who answered a knock at his own apartment in Fort Walton Beach holding a gun and was shot within seconds. Lead with the acquittal and the facts not in dispute — his own home, a legally held gun, seconds between the door opening and the shots. The mechanism: the verdict turns on what a jury accepts as an officer's reasonable fear, in a state where residents are entitled to answer their door armed, so the right to bear arms and the licence to shoot an armed man meet at the same doorway and the officer prevails. Give the charge, what each side argued, the family's response and whether any civil case continues. Dateline Fort Walton Beach.

stories.label: See where Trump's $90 checks to 20 million seniors are going
stories.summary: Trump says he will send one-time $90 payments this month to more than 20 million older Americans enrolled in Medicare Part B — roughly $1.8 billion, weeks before the November midterm elections. Lead with the amount, the number of recipients and the timing, then the mechanism the reader should check: which funds pay for it and under what authority, since Congress holds the power of the purse and the piece describes it as the latest in a series of pre-election disbursements of government money. Say who is excluded, what the White House gives as the reason (offsetting healthcare costs) and what critics and budget experts say about its legality. Give the total only if the sources state it; otherwise give the two figures. Skip the state-by-state map. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Local automakers voice concerns as imports of used cars surge in Sept
stories.summary: Used-car imports into Pakistan surged in September after the government eased the rules, following a brief dip when it abolished the Personal Baggage Scheme. Lead with the September figure against the previous months, as Dawn gives them, then the mechanism: Pakistan's car assemblers have operated for decades behind import barriers, and opening the door to used imports pits buyers who want cheaper cars against local plants and their jobs — while every imported car is paid for in dollars by a country with inflation above 10% and scarce reserves. Say which rule changed and why (state whether it is an IMF commitment only if Dawn does), what manufacturers and importers each argue, and what the duties are. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: North-east governors raise ₦10.8 billion to form regional airline
stories.summary: The six states of Nigeria's north-east have raised ₦10.8 billion in counterpart funding to launch a regional airline, Borno governor Babagana Zulum told the North East Governors' Forum in Maiduguri. Lead with the sum, who put it up and what it buys. The mechanism: this is the region emptied by the Boko Haram insurgency, where roads are unsafe and commercial carriers serve few routes, so state governments are pooling public money to build the link the market and the federal government have not — say which states contribute, who will operate the airline, when it is meant to fly, and what else the forum decided on security, as Premium Times reports. Note the record of state-owned airlines in Nigeria only if the article does. Dateline Maiduguri.

stories.label: Northrop Grumman’s Talon Blue Collaborative Combat Aircraft Has Flown
stories.summary: Northrop Grumman's Talon Blue, its entry for the US Air Force's Collaborative Combat Aircraft programme, has made its first flight. Lead with the flight — when, where, and what was demonstrated — then what the aircraft is: an uncrewed jet meant to fly alongside crewed fighters, carrying sensors or weapons at a fraction of a fighter's cost. The mechanism a technical reader wants: how much autonomy the aircraft has versus control from the fighter it accompanies, what it costs per airframe, and which competitors it is up against for the next production increment, as TWZ reports. Say what is confirmed by the company or the Air Force and what is TWZ's analysis. Dateline the test site the article names.

stories.label: IAF Chief rules out separate drone force, calls them evolutionary
stories.summary: India's air force chief, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, set out the service's position on Saturday: no separate drone force, a fighter fleet that is shrinking, delays in inducting the home-built Tejas, a need to fast-track the AMCA fifth-generation fighter against China's, and a multi-role fighter (MRFA) purchase that could be finalised in the 2026-27 fiscal year. Do not write it as a speech report. Lead with the hard numbers — squadron strength against the sanctioned figure, the Tejas delivery shortfall, the size of the MRFA order — then the mechanism: an air force that cannot get its domestic jet on time must buy abroad while its neighbours field fifth-generation aircraft, and its chief is saying drones do not close that gap. Say what is decided (a timeline for MRFA) and what is only his view. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Iranian center unveils projects to advance access to space
stories.summary: Nader Mokari, head of the Iranian Space Research Center, set out at a press conference the projects Iran is pursuing for cheaper and more reliable access to orbit, including work to reduce mission failures. The only source is Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency: attribute the plans to Mokari and to Mehr by name and state none of the capabilities as fact. Lead with the concrete items — which launchers, orbital-transfer or solid-propellant stages, which satellites and what dates — and the admission that failures need reducing. The mechanism: Iran is under sanctions and at war, so its space programme is built on domestic solid-fuel technology that overlaps with missile work, which is why outside governments watch each launch; say that only in one sentence and as context. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Recovery after intimate partner violence: New study reveals what works
stories.summary: A Dutch study examines what helps people recover after violence by a current or former partner, in a country where more than 1 million people aged 16 and over experience domestic violence each year. Lead with the finding — which forms of support were associated with recovery and which were not — and give the institution, the journal, the sample size and the method, as Phys.org reports them. The mechanism: say what the researchers think explains the difference (safety first, social support, professional help, time) only as far as the study does, and what it could not measure. A finding, not advice: no second-person guidance. Dateline the university's city.
